whatThePageStates: The page is a catalogue of the GuardDuty finding types that apply to Amazon S3 resources. An intro paragraph explains that a finding has a Resource Type of S3Bucket when its data source is CloudTrail data events for S3, or AccessKey when its data source is CloudTrail management events, and an Important callout says that findings sourced from CloudTrail data events for S3 are only generated when S3 Protection is enabled. A Topics list enumerates 20 finding-type identifiers, and each one then gets its own section with a plain-English title, a Default severity, a single Data source line, a description, and a Remediation recommendations paragraph. The page makes no statement about any finding type that GuardDuty does not support, and there are no tables, no Yes/No cells, and no Region or partition information anywhere on it.

features.statuses: 20 supported finding types, 0 not-supported; 20+0=20. Every entry on this page is a positive claim of existence - GuardDuty can generate this finding. Presence in the Topics list and a matching section is the only status signal the page carries; there is no No column, no 'not available' note, and no deprecated or retired marker. The Topics bullet count (20) equals the finding-type H2 count (20); the page has 21 H2 headings in total, the extra one being the trailing 'See also' section, which is not a finding type. Severity splits 11 High, 4 Low, 5 Medium = 20, and severity is an attribute of each finding, not a coverage status.
features.scope: Two-dimensional in one respect only: each finding names exactly one Data source, splitting 15 findings on 'CloudTrail data events for S3' and 5 on 'CloudTrail management events' (15+5=20). The Important callout makes that split load-bearing - the 15 data-event findings are generated only if S3 Protection is enabled, while the 5 management-event findings come from GuardDuty's foundational source. The same split drives the stated Resource Type (S3Bucket for the 15, AccessKey for the 5). There is no per-Region, per-partition, or per-plan dimension on this page.
features.reasoning: findingType is the axis because the enumerated things are GuardDuty's own published finding-type identifiers (Discovery:S3/AnomalousBehavior, Policy:S3/BucketPublicAccessGranted, and so on), a catalogue GuardDuty publishes about itself rather than an external universe. The unit of claim is one finding-type identifier, which is exactly what the Topics list enumerates and exactly what each H2 names, so rows do not collapse - 20 sections name 20 distinct identifiers with no duplicates.

shouldNotExtract: The trailing 'See also' section is AI-coding-assistant boilerplate about the Agent Toolkit for AWS skills catalogue and is not coverage - it also contributes a 21st H2 that must not be counted as a finding type. The '### ...' sub-headings under each finding are prose titles (An S3 API was invoked from a Tor exit node IP address), not separate finding types, so counting all headings doubles the total. 'Default severity: High/Medium/Low' is a severity attribute, not a coverage status. The Important callout about S3 Protection auto-enable dates, the two identical Note blocks about Zelkova, deny-all policies and effectivePermission=UNKNOWN, the 'Remediation recommendations' headings that repeat under every finding, the example API names in backticks (ListObjects, GetObjectAcl, GetObject, CopyObject, PutObject, PutObjectAcl, DeleteBucket), and the cross-page links (guardduty_data-sources.md, compromised-s3.md, s3-protection.md, Zelkova blog, S3 user-guide pages) are all context, not enumerable coverage.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no Region table, and no partition; any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: implicitly Amazon S3 only - the page is scoped to one service and does not enumerate services, so it supports no service-count claim beyond 1. RESOURCE TYPE: only a passing prose statement that findings carry a Resource Type of S3Bucket or AccessKey depending on the data source; that is 2 mentioned resource types describing finding shape, not a coverage enumeration of resource types, and it should not be reported as resource-type coverage. The one dimension the page genuinely supplies is the finding-type catalogue (20) and its data-source split (15 CloudTrail data events for S3 / 5 CloudTrail management events).
trap: The likeliest misparse is counting headings instead of finding types: the page has 21 H2 headings (20 findings plus 'See also') and 20 H3 prose titles, so a naive heading sweep yields 21, 40 or 41 instead of 20. Runners-up: (a) treating the severity words as coverage statuses and reporting 11 Yes / 9 something-else, when severity says nothing about support; (b) inventing not-supported entries - this page never states that any finding type is unavailable, so the No count is 0, not an inferred remainder; (c) flattening away the data-source scope and claiming all 20 are always generated, when 15 of them require S3 Protection to be enabled; (d) harvesting the S3Bucket/AccessKey sentence as a resourceType coverage axis of 2; (e) harvesting the backticked example API names as an apiOperation axis.
